title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Ni(II), the 3d ion most often used in these IDA 3d-4f clusters, is a poor choice for single-molecule magnets because of its relatively low spin and weak magnetic anisotropy.
explanation: The review notes SMM interest for 3d-4f clusters but explicitly contrasts Ni(II) with more anisotropic ions such as Fe(III) or Mn(IV). Better SMM behavior would require other 3d ions and ligand optimization.
scope: SMM design within IDA-stabilized 3d-4f clusters that commonly use Ni(II).
caveats: This is a design limitation stated by the review, not a survey of measured energy barriers for the tabulated clusters.
